$comment: Shared by workers/uw-frame/src/lib/frameQuality.ts (the worker) and scripts/cam_seaweed.py (the vision reader). One file, so the two cannot drift.

A frame is BLANK when the middle of the picture is a flat dark GREY and nothing in it is brighter than that: YouTube's black slate (what a live stream shows while it sends no video), the player's loading spinner on black, a 'Video unavailable' page. Measured 2026-10-17 on 60+ such frames from the cam archive and the live worker: every one has a mean brightness of 17.3-20.9 and a 95th percentile of 22-25 (of 255).

A real frame that is merely dark is NOT blank. Real night frames measured: underwater cam before dawn mean 8.7 (95th percentile 11), Boca feed cam at night mean 0.1-5.7, a dim feed frame mean 14.5 (95th percentile 26), the floodlit Deerfield pier at night 95th percentile 45 or more. Black is darker than YouTube's grey, so the two groups do not overlap.

blankP95Below: the 95th-percentile brightness of the region's 8x8 blocks must be under this (nothing bright in the picture). blankMeanAtLeast: and the region's mean must be at least this (YouTube's grey, not true black). Both must hold. The two measured groups sit 1.3 apart on the mean (14.5 real vs 17.3 blank), so look at a new cam's frames before moving this.

minBytes: below this the upload is a stub or truncated, whatever it shows. A black 720p frame from ffmpeg is 12,815 bytes, so a size floor cannot separate black from dark: the picture check does that. maxBytes: the biggest upload the worker takes.

richBytes: a frame this large has detail everywhere; no blank frame measured is over 40,000 bytes, so the worker skips the pixel check (and its CPU cost on the free plan's 10 ms limit). Set it to null to always check. Real dark night frames can be 57,000 bytes because of sensor noise, so the pixel check, not the size, decides.

region: the part of the frame (fractions of width and height) that the statistics read. It leaves out the YouTube player's top bar (title, mute, settings) and bottom bar (Live badge, progress line, share, More videos), and the cam owner's overlay lines.
